terra.problem: The verse calls for confessions, but it does not say that nobody has to bring a gift or that only words are required.
“They hand the whole pile over” presents Israel as actually making the request. The passage gives them words to say.
The words say Assyria will not save Israel; they do not say Israel will no longer lean on Assyria.
Calling Assyria a powerful nation adds a Bible fact from outside the passage without a reference.

The descriptions of Babylon as a city and empire and Assyria as a powerful nation add Bible facts from outside the passage without references.
The lopsided-cookie joke makes Israel's idol worship the target of the laugh, making light of serious sin.
The explanation calls the fatherless finding compassion the reason Israel gives for turning to the LORD. The passage does not specify that connection.
“After a stumble and a confession” presents the confession as having happened. Israel is told to bring confessions and given words to say.
“Free love” has a well-known second meaning and is a prohibited kind of phrase.
Papa says he holds a grudge, contradicting the rule that he never holds one.
Papa cannot step outside barefoot. His gold base is part of him and always comes with him.
“Then Israel starts to blossom” presents the promised blossoming as something that happens, rather than retaining the verse's future wording.
The line saying one cannot say such a thing about thorns does not make sense: thorns can grow too.
The passage addresses Ephraim as Israel, so identifying Ephraim only as one tribe is misleading here. The claim that idols cannot answer is also not stated in this passage.
The claims that Ephraim is a tribe and that idols cannot answer need references because they come from outside this passage.
